reflection.text:
The dose descent correctly isolated a specific low-dose phenotype from high-dose toxicity: at 0.1 uM cells were enlarged/flat with high frac_multinucleate_proxy and frac_large_nucleus (e13), persisting as frac_large_nucleus z=+61.1 at 1 uM (e5) and visually confirmed as lower density with enlarged/multinucleate morphology (e15), while the 10 uM well had only 6 cells with extreme roundness (e2). Separating low-dose (e17) from top-dose (e18) atlas comparisons was the right acquisition choice to avoid pooling toxic effects.
The error was treating enlarged/irregular/multinucleate nuclei as Aurora-specific cytokinesis failure. Topoisomerase II inhibition/DNA replication stress can also produce enlarged nuclei, polyploidy and secondary mitotic failure, but DNA replication was set to 0.05 early and never recovered, and the 0-hit second literature search for topo II multinucleation reinforced the miss. I overweighted the 6/10 Aurora low-dose atlas hit (e17) and microscopist Aurora calls (e15, e6) and underweighted that protein synthesis 4/10 (e7) and microtubule stabilizer 7/10 (e18) were unstable across doses and that dose-response trends for large-nucleus, multinucleate proxy and DNA content were non-significant and underpowered (e9-e12).
In retrospect the discriminating feature was not size alone but DNA synthesis versus mitosis: the planned phospho-H3 plus polyploidy test was insufficient without a replication/DNA-damage arm for a topo II/DNA inhibitor.

Failed to test DNA replication inhibition directly: dose_response for nuc_dna_integrated and cell_count were negative trends with p=0.2 (e11, e12) but underpowered with 4 wells, and no EdU/gamma-H2AX measurement was acquired to distinguish topo II-induced replication arrest from mitotic failure.

Verdict: approve.

Top call is favored by the specific low-dose phenotype, not the nonspecific high-dose toxicity. At 0.1 µM (e13, dose idx3 rep1) cells are enlarged/flat (cell_area z=+13.1, major-axis z=+14.9, roundness z=-19.1) with frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+15.3 and frac_large_nucleus z=+12.5, visually confirmed as bi-/multinucleate cytokinesis-failure morphology (e15), and the low-dose atlas is 6/10 Aurora (e17). ## Unblinding

Compound: **mitoxantrone** (PubChem CID [4212](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/4212))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor; DNA inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **Aurora kinase inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA replication**.

## Reflection

The dose descent correctly isolated a specific low-dose phenotype from high-dose toxicity: at 0.1 uM cells were enlarged/flat with high frac_multinucleate_proxy and frac_large_nucleus (e13), persisting as frac_large_nucleus z=+61.1 at 1 uM (e5) and visually confirmed as lower density with enlarged/multinucleate morphology (e15), while the 10 uM well had only 6 cells with extreme roundness (e2). Separating low-dose (e17) from top-dose (e18) atlas comparisons was the right acquisition choice to avoid pooling toxic effects.
The error was treating enlarged/irregular/multinucleate nuclei as Aurora-specific cytokinesis failure. Topoisomerase II inhibition/DNA replication stress can also produce enlarged nuclei, polyploidy and secondary mitotic failure, but DNA replication was set to 0.05 early and never recovered, and the 0-hit second literature search for topo II multinucleation reinforced the miss. I overweighted the 6/10 Aurora low-dose atlas hit (e17) and microscopist Aurora calls (e15, e6) and underweighted that protein synthesis 4/10 (e7) and microtubule stabilizer 7/10 (e18) were unstable across doses and that dose-response trends for large-nucleus, multinucleate proxy and DNA content were non-significant and underpowered (e9-e12).
In retrospect the discriminating feature was not size alone but DNA synthesis versus mitosis: the planned phospho-H3 plus polyploidy test was insufficient without a replication/DNA-damage arm for a topo II/DNA inhibitor.

What was right:
- Detected reproducible enlarged-nucleus / large-flat-cell phenotype from 0.1 uM (e13) through 0.3-3 uM (e3, e4, e5) with replicate confirmation at 1 uM (e14).
- Recognized 10 uM rounded phenotype (e2, e16) as 6-cell likely toxic effect distinct from low-dose phenotype and downweighted microtubule stabilizer 7/10 top-dose match (e18).
- Used dose descent to 0.1 uM and separate low- vs high-dose atlas comparisons (e17 vs e18) plus visual checks (e15) instead of relying only on pooled 1-3 uM atlas (e7).

What was wrong or missed:
- Misattributed frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+15.3 and frac_large_nucleus z=+12.5 to +61.1 (e13, e5) and microscopist bi/multinucleate description (e15) specifically to Aurora kinase inhibition.
- Overweighted 6/10 Aurora atlas match at low dose (e17) while discounting 1/10 DNA replication signal in same comparison and early DNA replication/DNA damage probabilities of 0.05.
- Failed to test DNA replication inhibition directly: dose_response for nuc_dna_integrated and cell_count were negative trends with p=0.2 (e11, e12) but underpowered with 4 wells, and no EdU/gamma-H2AX measurement was acquired to distinguish topo II-induced replication arrest from mitotic failure.

Proposed next experiment: EdU incorporation plus gamma-H2AX and phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 with DNA-content flow cytometry to test for DNA replication inhibition/DNA damage versus Aurora mitotic phenotype, with mitoxantrone versus etoposide and an Aurora inhibitor as references.
